hook.en: When something goes wrong, does anyone ever say, "It was my fault"? In Melon City, everyone points at someone else.

objectives.en: Explain how the architect shifts the blame to the king
Identify what the chain of blame satirises

narration.en: When something goes wrong, does anyone ever say, "It was my fault"? In Melon City, everyone points at someone else.

body.en: Furious, the king orders the chief of builders to be hanged. The chief blames the workmen; the workmen blame the masons for making bricks of the wrong size; the masons blame the architect. Each group escapes by pointing at the next.

narration.en: Furious, the king orders the chief of builders to be hanged. The chief blames the workmen; the workmen blame the masons for making bricks of the wrong size; the masons blame the architect. Each group escapes by pointing at the next.
We draw the chain of blame as a flowchart that loops back to the king.

say.en: The king orders the chief builder to be hanged.
The chief builder blames the workmen.
The workmen blame the masons for wrong-sized bricks.
The architect says the king changed the plans.
The blame returns to the king, who is confused.

body.en: The architect reminds the king that he himself had made changes to the plans. The blame has come full circle, and the king is confused. Seth uses this circular chain to mock people who never accept responsibility and a system where punishment is decided before the facts.

points.en: Architect: the king amended the plans
Blame returns to the king himself
Satire: passing the buck; hasty justice

narration.en: The architect reminds the king that he himself had made changes to the plans. The blame has come full circle, and the king is confused. Seth uses this circular chain to mock people who never accept responsibility and a system where punishment is decided before the facts.

problem.en: Trace the chain of blame after the arch knocked off the king's crown.

steps.en: Chief builder → workmen → masons (wrong-sized bricks) → architect.
Architect → the king himself, who had changed the plans.

answer.en: The king ordered the chief builder hanged; the chief blamed the workmen, who blamed the masons for the size of the bricks; the masons blamed the architect, and the architect blamed the king, who had amended the plans.

body.en: The blame goes round in a circle and comes back to where it started: King, Chief builder, Workmen, Masons, Architect, King.
